title: Work
intro: Working with Chinese colleagues and clients: titles, introductions, WeChat, meetings and writing.

scenes.title: Titles and forms of address
scenes.description: How to address superiors, colleagues, clients and groups at work: surname + title (王总, 李经理, 王主任, 王工), surname + 先生/女士, 您 vs 你, familiar 老X/小X, addressing a group (各位, 诸位, 您二位), and what not to say (您们).

phrases.pinyin_as_source: nín (现代汉语词典; HSK 2025 L1); nin2 (CC-CEDICT)
phrases.english: you (polite form)
phrases.usage: The respectful 'you'. 现代汉语词典 glosses 您 as 你；你们（含敬意） and calls it the 尊称 (respectful form) of 你; CC-CEDICT: 'you (courteous, as opposed to informal 你)'. In the official workplace dialogues it is used upward and to clients: staff to a general manager 李总，请您在这份文件上签字 (BCT A); a new employee to the boss 谢谢您！谢谢您给我这个机会 (HSK 3); a host to a visiting manager 您好，王经理 (HSK 5). The superior answers with 你 (欢迎你来公司工作) and peers use 你. Use 您 with superiors, clients, older people and at first meetings. 您 takes no -们 (see rule on 您们). When 您 starts to sound too distant with a colleague was not verified in this session.
phrases.speaker: either
phrases.regional_note: Possible north/south differences in how often 您 is used (relevant for a family from south/central China) were not verified in this session.

phrases.pinyin_as_source: zong3 (CC-CEDICT 总); lǎozǒnɡ (现代汉语词典 老总)
phrases.literal: Wang + chief (short for 总经理 general manager, 总编 etc.)
phrases.english: Mr./Ms. Wang (to a general manager or other '总' executive)
phrases.usage: Surname + 总 for people whose title contains 总: 总经理 (general manager), 总编辑 (editor-in-chief), 总工程师 (chief engineer). CC-CEDICT 总: '(after a person's name) abbr. for 总经理 or 总编 etc'; 现代汉语词典 老总: 也称有总工程师、总经理、总编辑等头衔的人（多和姓连用）. Used to the person's face (李总，请您在这份文件上签字) and when referring to them in emails (王总希望能在11月与李总见面), both in the CLEC BCT (A) sample. Gender-neutral. Combine with 您. Slot: the surname (王总 is a slot example; 李总 is in the source). Whether staff also use 总 for executives without 总 in their title was not verified.
phrases.speaker: either

phrases.pinyin_as_source: xiānsheng (HSK 2025 L1); xian1 sheng5 (CC-CEDICT); xiān•shenɡ (现代汉语词典)
phrases.english: Mr. Wang
phrases.usage: Surname + 先生: the general respectful way to address a man when you do not use a job title (现代汉语词典 先生 ❷: 对知识分子和有一定身份的成年男子的尊称). BCT (A): 王先生，您好！今晚的宴会在华丰饭店举行。 — reply 好的，到时候见。; HSK 5: 请问先生您怎么称呼？ — 我姓李。 — 李先生，里面请; letter: 张先生：您好！ (Hanban BCT A sample of c. 2013). In a formal letter to an unknown person: 总经理先生/女士：您好！ (Hanban BCT B sample of c. 2013). Careful: after a pronoun, 先生 means 'husband' (她先生, 现代汉语词典 ❸).
phrases.speaker: either

phrases.pinyin_as_source: lǎoshī (HSK 2025 L1; 现代汉语词典); lao3 shi1 (CC-CEDICT)
phrases.english: Teacher Zhang (Mr./Ms. Zhang)
phrases.usage: Surname + 老师. The 2025 HSK syllabus gives 姓氏+职业（张老师） as its model of a Chinese form of address. 现代汉语词典 defines 老师 as 对教师的尊称，泛指传授文化、技术的人或在某方面值得学习的人, so beyond schoolteachers it extends to trainers, experts and people one learns from. How widely 老师 is used today as a general courtesy title for colleagues, media people or clients was NOT verified in this session (open question). Phone example: 喂，是王老师吗？ (GF 0025-2021).
phrases.speaker: either

phrases.english: (young) Zhang: familiar form for a younger or junior colleague
phrases.usage: 小 + surname is an affectionate, familiar form (新华字典/汉典 data: 小 用在姓、名、排行等之前，表示爱称). In the official workplace texts it is said by a manager or colleague to a junior: 小张，你这份计划书写得不错，就按照这个计划去做市场调查吧 (HSK 4, a manager to an employee); 小林，这次的招聘是由你负责吧？ (HSK 4); a note from 王东: 小张，我去三楼会议室开会了 (Hanban BCT A sample of c. 2013). You may hear it used for you if you are junior. Not a title: do not use it for superiors, clients or older people (see rule; this direction is inferred from the sources, which never show it used upward).

rules.rule: At work, address people as surname + job title or profession (王总, 李经理, 王主任, 王工, 王律师, 张老师), or surname + 先生/女士 when no title is used; keep the same form when referring to them (王总希望…). Being able to use Chinese forms of address correctly is listed as a basic workplace communication skill.
rules.why: The 2025 HSK syllabus teaches 姓氏+职业（张老师） as the standard pattern for 称谓语; the official business tests (BCT) and HSK dialogues use it throughout; the vocational Chinese standard T/ISCLT 002-2023 lists correct use of 称谓语 as an entry-level workplace strategy.

rules.rule: Use 您 to superiors, clients, older people and people you meet in a formal setting. In the official dialogues superiors answer with 你, and colleagues of the same level use 你 with each other.
rules.why: 现代汉语词典 calls 您 the 尊称 of 你. Official dialogues show the asymmetry: boss → new employee 欢迎你来公司工作, employee → boss 谢谢您！谢谢您给我这个机会 (HSK 3); staff → general manager 李总，请您在这份文件上签字 (BCT A); manager → junior 小林，这次的招聘是由你负责吧？ (HSK 4); employee → boss on the phone 我马上让她联系您 (HSK 5).
rules.regional_note: North/south differences in how much 您 is used were not verified in this session.

rules.rule: Do not say 您们. For two people say 您二位 or 您俩, for three 您三位 or 您仨, for more 您诸位, or address the group with 各位 / 诸位. Plain 你们 is also normal: a guest thanks the hosts with 谢谢你们的热情招待.
rules.why: Dictionary note (新华字典/汉典 data): 您 用于多数时不加词尾“们”; 现代汉语词典 glosses 您 itself as 你；你们（含敬意） (example 您二位想吃点儿什么？) and has no entry 您们; the GF 0025-2021 list of personal pronouns (我、你、您、他、她、我们、你们、他们、她们) has no 您们. 您们 does occur in real text, but rarely: OpenSubtitles 2018 zh_cn counts 您们 136 vs 你们 207,368; the jieba lexicon lists 您们 with frequency 20 vs 你们 21,386. So you may see it, but it is not the standard form.

rules.rule: 老 + surname (老王) and 小 + surname (小张) are familiar forms, not titles. 老 marks familiarity; 小 is an affectionate form, and in the official workplace texts 小X is always said by a manager or colleague to a junior or younger person (小张，你这份计划书写得不错…; 小林，这次的招聘是由你负责吧？), while colleagues call each other 老王.
rules.why: Dictionary senses: 老 前缀，用于称人 (现代汉语词典), 'to indicate affection or familiarity' (CC-CEDICT); 小 用在姓、名、排行等之前，表示爱称 (新华字典/汉典 data). Usage pattern from the official HSK 4 and BCT samples.

rules.rule: Do not call a superior, a client or an older person 小X (or 老X); use their title (王总, 李经理, 王主任…) with 您.
rules.why: Inference only: 小X is an affectionate form used downward in every official example seen, 老X is familiar, and the same texts address superiors with title + 您. No source seen in this session states this prohibition explicitly; re-check with a teaching source.

rules.rule: To address a woman formally, use surname + 女士 or her job title. Be careful with 小姐: besides 'Miss', CC-CEDICT records a slang sense 'prostitute'. Older official material still uses 小姐 neutrally (HSK 5 sample: 小姐，你好，我是来应聘的; 是王小姐让我下午两点半来面试的), so you will meet it in textbooks; how acceptable it is in mainland workplaces today was not verified in this session.
rules.why: 现代汉语词典: 女士 对妇女的尊称; 小姐 (5th-edition text) 对年轻的女子或未出嫁的女子的称呼; CC-CEDICT 小姐: young lady; miss; (slang) prostitute.

phrases.english: Hello everyone, I'm Zhang Ming, a student at Peking University.
phrases.usage: Model self-introduction to a group (CLEC YCT 4 sample): 你先做个自我介绍吧。 — 大家好，我叫张明，是北京大学的学生。 Frame: 大家好 + 我叫 [name] + 是 [organisation] 的 [role]. At work, fill the slots with your company and role (a slot change; the exact work version 我是X公司的Y was not seen in a source in this session). Related official form: 我姓李，是各位的导游。 (HSK 4). A first-day self-introduction at a meeting is a task in the official BCT speaking sample (你今天入职，和同事一起开会，你会怎样介绍自己？).

phrases.english: Oh, not at all. (modest reply to a compliment)
phrases.usage: Modest deflection of praise: 现代汉语词典 哪里 ❺ 谦辞，用来婉转地推辞对自己的褒奖 (example: “你这篇文章写得真好！”“～，～！”); CC-CEDICT 哪里哪里: you're too kind; you flatter me. Official Hanban BCT (A) sample of c. 2013: 大家都说你是公司里最好的员工。 — 哪里哪里。 Whether it now sounds dated or textbook-like was NOT verified in this session; sourced alternatives: 您过奖了, 不敢当. Pronunciation: written nǎlǐ (CC-CEDICT, HSK 2025); in speech 哪 becomes rising before 里 (third-tone sandhi) and 现代汉语词典 marks 里 as usually light (nǎ•lǐ).

rules.rule: Shaking hands at work: stand up (rise if you are seated), lean slightly forward, offer your right hand at about one metre, smile and look at the person; shake for 2-3 seconds, moving 2-3 times, palm to palm, with a moderate grip. The superior offers his or her hand first to a subordinate; between a man and a woman the woman offers first (if she does not, the man nods); with several people go by status or age, or simply from nearest to farthest.
rules.why: Business-etiquette reading passage in the CLEC BCT (B) sample paper ('以下是关于握手的一些商务礼仪').

sources.title: 商务中文考试 BCT（B）样卷
sources.publisher: 教育部中外语言交流合作中心 (copy in docrealm/docs-hsk)
sources.evidence: A 在职场生涯中，握手是一种友好的象征，更是一种交流的形式。握手时应该站立，如果已经落座，在即将与人握手时也应该马上站起来，身体稍微前倾，以此来表示对对方的尊敬。 B …在距离对方一米左右的地方伸出右手，握住对方的右手，同时面带微笑，眼睛要注视对方… C 女士同男士握手时，应由女士先伸手。如果女士没有握手的意愿，男士可点头致意。上级同下级握手时，则应由上级首先伸手。一人与多人握手时，顺序既可以根据地位或年龄而定，也可以由近及远依次进行。 D 握手的时间应为两到三秒，上下晃动两三次，然后自然松开。握手时应该手掌对手掌，不能指尖对指尖。 (two-column layout reconstructed)

rules.rule: Answer praise with a modest formula (谦辞) such as 您过奖了 or 不敢当; 哪里哪里 is the textbook form (its present-day naturalness is an open question).
rules.why: 现代汉语词典 gives 过奖 and 不敢当 as its examples of 谦辞 (表示谦虚的言辞，如“过奖、不敢当”等) and lists 哪里 ❺ as a 谦辞 declining praise; the official Hanban BCT (A) sample of c. 2013 answers 大家都说你是公司里最好的员工 with 哪里哪里; GF 0025-2021: 您千万别这样说，我实在是不敢当。

rules.rule: 幸会, 久仰 and 指教 are fixed courtesies (客套话) for first meetings and formal settings. 幸会 counts as core business vocabulary (BCT A list); 久仰 is advanced (HSK 7-9) and rarer; the plain greetings of the official samples (很高兴认识你, HSK 1; 您好，很高兴见到您, BCT A) do the same job at a basic level.
rules.why: 现代汉语词典 labels 久仰 (初次见面时说), 幸会 and 指教 ❷ as 客套话; 幸会 is on the BCT (A) 600-word list; 久仰 is HSK 7-9 in the 2025 syllabus; subtitle counts: 幸会 1,676, 久仰 137.

rules.rule: 面子 ('face') is a person's public standing and self-esteem. People avoid situations where they could 丢面子 (lose face), and favours are sometimes granted 看在X的面子上 ('out of regard for X'). Practical consequence (inference, not stated as a rule in the sources seen): avoid embarrassing someone in front of others, e.g. correcting a superior or client publicly.
rules.why: 现代汉语词典 面子 ❷ 表面的虚荣：爱～｜要～｜你这话伤了他的～ ❸ 情面：给～｜碍于～，只好答应了; HSK 6 sample: 很多人不敢当众讲话，是怕说错话被人瞧不起，丢面子; GF 0025-2021: 我是看在她的面子上才答应的; the 2025 HSK syllabus teaches the fixed pattern 看在X的面子上.

rules.rule: Business phone calls: avoid calling before 7:00, after 22:00, at dinner time, or at midday if the person naps; keep calls short (about 3-5 minutes) and prepare your points. Open with 您好, use 请 often, close with 谢谢. Answer before the third ring or apologise (对不起，让您久等了). When answering, introduce yourself first, then politely ask who is calling; if the person asked for is absent, offer to take a message. Do not eat, drink or talk to others during the call.
rules.why: Reading passage on business phone etiquette in the Hanban BCT (B) sample paper (c. 2013, early WeChat era; still the only phone-etiquette source seen in this session).

sources.title: 商务汉语考试 BCT（B）样卷 BCTB0001
sources.publisher: 孔子学院总部/国家汉办 (copy in docrealm/docs-hsk)
sources.evidence: A 打商务电话应尽量避免在上午7点以前或晚上10点以后，也最好不要在晚饭时间打电话。如果对方有午休习惯，中午不要打扰他。电话交谈的时间不宜过长，一般3-5分钟最佳。 B 打商务电话前，要核实对方公司或单位的名称、电话号码以及接话人姓名。为了保证通话顺利，应提前写出交谈要点… C 打商务电话要用“您好”开头，多说“请”字，以“谢谢”收尾。通话态度要亲和，声音大小要适中，始终保持微笑。严忌通话时吃东西、喝水或与第三者交谈。商务电话要在铃响三遍前接听，否则就要道歉：“对不起，让您久等了。” D 一般接听商务电话时，要先做自我介绍，然后礼貌地询问对方身份。如果对方找的人在你身旁，要跟对方说：“请稍等”，然后用手掩住话筒，将电话转给他人接听。如果对方找的人不在，应主动询问是否需要留言。 (two-column layout reconstructed)

rules.rule: Business emails and letters: start with surname + title + colon and 您好！ (黄经理：您好！ / 吴秘书：您好！); if you do not know the name, 总经理先生/女士：您好！. Refer to the other side with 贵 (贵公司, 贵方). When sending documents or goods add 请注意查收; close with an offer such as 有需要的话，请您和我们联系, then company/name and date.
rules.why: Model business emails and letters in the official BCT sample papers (CLEC BCT A; Hanban BCT A/B samples of c. 2013).

rules.rule: When someone calls for a colleague who is out, don't stop at 没有 / 不清楚 / 不知道: offer to have the colleague contact them (我马上让她联系您) or offer someone else who can help (这里有小张、小王还有我，您需要哪一位？).

scenes.title: Meetings: opening, running and closing
scenes.description: Opening and chairing a meeting, asking for and giving views, adding a point, agreeing and deciding, closing, and the small talk around a meeting with visitors. Built only from official HSK/BCT test material, the 2021 national grammar standard, 现代汉语词典 and CC-CEDICT (web search was unavailable this session); several common target phrases from the brief (我们开始吧, 我补充一点, 我有个问题, 今天就到这里) could not be verified and are listed in open_questions.

phrases.pinyin: Zuò hǎo ba, yào kāihuì le.
phrases.literal: sit well + suggestion-particle, about-to hold-meeting + particle
phrases.english: Please take your seats, the meeting is about to start.
phrases.usage: A natural way for the person chairing to get a meeting going: 好 after a verb means the action is properly done (坐好 'be seated'), 要…了 means 'is about to'. This is the dictionary's own example (现代汉语词典, entry 好 ❼). A firmer variant from the same dictionary (entry 大家): 大家安静点儿，现在开会了 (Dàjiā ānjìng diǎnr, xiànzài kāihuì le) 'Everyone, a bit quieter please, the meeting is starting'. The brief's 我们开始吧 'let's begin' was not found in any source seen this session.

phrases.pinyin: Jīntiān de huìyì, zhǔnbèi yánjiū sān gè zhòngyào wèntí.
phrases.literal: today 's meeting, plan consider three (measure) important issue
phrases.english: At today's meeting we plan to discuss three important issues.
phrases.usage: Announcing the agenda. In meetings 研究 means 'consider / discuss (an issue)', not 'do research': 现代汉语词典 研究 ❷ 考虑或商讨（意见、问题）, with exactly this example. Change the number as needed. For a single topic the same dictionary has 这次会议专门讨论了资金问题 'this meeting dealt specifically with funding' (entry 专门). The brief's 今天我们主要讨论… was not found in any source seen this session.

phrases.english: First …, then …
phrases.usage: Frame for walking people through steps or agenda points. The national grammar standard lists 首先……，然后…… (level 3) with the example 我们首先要找到科学的练习方法，然后坚持每天练习 'first we must find a scientific way to practise, then keep practising every day', and 首先……，其次…… (level 4, 'first …, second …'), e.g. 首先我们要读一遍课文，其次我们要根据课文做一个练习. Fill in your own clauses.
phrases.speaker: me

examples: 我们首先要找到科学的练习方法，然后坚持每天练习。

phrases.hanzi: 以上是这次活动的计划，看看大家还有什么意见。
phrases.pinyin: Yǐshàng shì zhè cì huódòng de jìhuà, kànkan dàjiā hái yǒu shénme yìjiàn.
phrases.literal: above is this time event 's plan, look-look everyone still have what opinion
phrases.english: That's the plan for this event. Let's see if anyone has any comments.
phrases.usage: Wrapping up a presentation and inviting input (official HSK 4 dialogue). 以上是… 'the above is…'. 意见 means views or suggestions, but can also mean objections or complaints (现代汉语词典 意见 ❶❷), so 有意见 can signal dissatisfaction. Reply you may hear: 我觉得安排得很好，由你来组织我们都很放心 (next item). Put what you presented in the slot.
phrases.speaker: me

phrases.english: Please tell us what you think.
phrases.usage: Inviting someone to give their opinion. It is the standard wording of opinion questions in current official speaking tests (2025 new HSK level 5: 你是怎么理解这句话的？请谈谈你的看法。; HSKK advanced: 你同意吗？请谈谈你的看法。). phrases.usage: A polite way to say 'I have a question' to someone senior or more expert: 请教 = ask for guidance (现代汉语词典: 请求指教). rules.rule: In business settings the more senior person offers a hand first (上级同下级握手时，则应由上级首先伸手); between a woman and a man, the woman offers first; when shaking hands with several people, go by status or age, or simply from the nearest person outwards. Stand to shake hands (if seated, rise), lean slightly forward, smile and look at the person; about 2-3 seconds, two or three shakes, moderate firmness, palm to palm.
rules.why: Stated in a business-etiquette reading text of the current official Business Chinese Test sample (CLEC). It matters at the start of meetings with senior counterparts.

rules.rule: Chinese has set politeness formulas (客套话) for ending a presentation of your own work by inviting correction or comments, e.g. 有不对的地方请大家指正 or 有不完备的地方，请多提意见.
rules.why: 现代汉语词典 defines 指正 ❷ as a 客套话 'used to ask people to criticise one's own work or views' and gives these examples. Leaving it out is not an error, but using it sounds modest and polished.

Official HSK 4 dialogue: 我上午发的那份传真你收到了吧？ 'You got the fax I sent this morning, right?' and the reply 没收到。等等，我看一下，抱歉，没纸了，麻烦您再发一遍吧 'Didn't get it. Wait, let me look. Sorry, it's out of paper; could you send it again?' The 2025 new HSK sample has another 麻烦你 request: 麻烦你跟房东再谈谈，看能否便宜一些？

phrases.hanzi: 你的文件我打不开，你能再给我发一下儿吗？
phrases.pinyin: Nǐ de wénjiàn wǒ dǎ bù kāi, nǐ néng zài gěi wǒ fā yīxiàr ma?
phrases.literal: your file I open-not-able, you can again to me send a-bit (question particle)
phrases.english: I can't open your file. Could you send it to me again?
phrases.usage: Everyday work request (official example sentence in the national grammar standard). 能…吗 turns it into a request and V + 一下儿 softens it ('just quickly'). The standard writes 一下儿; the 2025 HSK word list has 一下 without 儿; both are standard. 打不开 'can't open': 不 is written bù (citation tone) though it is unstressed in speech.

phrases.literal: you see this method good not good
phrases.english: What do you think of this approach?
phrases.usage: Proposing something while leaving the decision to the other person: 你看… 'in your judgement' (现代汉语词典 看 ❷ 观察并加以判断, with this example). To a senior or client say 您看…. Related tag pattern from the national grammar standard: statement + 可以吗 / 好吗？, e.g. 你明天早点儿来，可以吗？ The brief's 您看…可以吗？ was not found verbatim this session.

phrases.pinyin: Fāngbiàn de shíhou, nǐ gěi wǒ huí gè diànhuà.
phrases.literal: convenient (de) time, you to me return a phone-call
phrases.english: Give me a call back when it's convenient.
phrases.usage: 方便 'convenient, suitable' (现代汉语词典 方便 ❸ 适宜, with this example). Leaving the timing to the other person makes the request polite. phrases.pinyin: Zhè piān gǎozi nín fèishén kànkan ba.
phrases.english: Could I trouble you to take a look at this draft?
phrases.usage: Asking a senior colleague to review your text. 费神 'spend effort' is used as a 客套话 when asking a favour (现代汉语词典, with this example), and 看看 softens the verb. Other formulas with the same function in the same dictionary: 劳神 (劳神代为照顾一下) and 有劳 (这件事有劳您了 'thank you for taking this on').

phrases.english: Thanks for your hard work. / Sorry to put this on you.
phrases.usage: Said when handing someone a demanding task, or thanking them for it. Official HSK 4 example: a colleague asks 小王 to translate a document by 10 pm and print it for the manager, ending with 辛苦你了. 现代汉语词典 lists 辛苦 ❷ as a 客套话 used when asking someone to do something (这事儿还得您辛苦一趟). With a senior person or client you would use 您 (辛苦您了, not attested in a source seen this session); whether juniors should say 辛苦了 to superiors could not be verified (open_questions).
phrases.speaker: either

phrases.pinyin: Shénme máfan bù máfan, wǒmen zhījiān bùyòng zhème kèqi.
phrases.literal: what trouble not trouble, we between no-need so polite
phrases.english: Trouble? Not at all. No need to be so formal between us.
phrases.usage: A warm reply you may hear after you apologise for the trouble or thank someone (official example in the national grammar standard; 什么 A 不 A dismisses the other person's word). Another reply to thanks in 现代汉语词典 (entry 好说): 好说，您太客气了 (Hǎoshuō, nín tài kèqi le) 'Don't mention it, you're too kind'.

phrases.english: Sorry to have kept you waiting.
phrases.usage: Apologising for a delay, on the phone, in person or when replying late. It is the 现代汉语词典 example for 对不起, and the official BCT business-telephone text says that if you don't answer before the third ring you must apologise with exactly these words. 不好意思 (bù hǎoyìsi) is a softer 'sorry' (next item).

phrases.hanzi: 东西倒是好东西，就是价钱太贵。
phrases.pinyin: Dōngxi dàoshi hǎo dōngxi, jiùshì jiàqian tài guì.
phrases.literal: thing admittedly good thing, just-is price too expensive
phrases.english: It's a good product all right, it's just too expensive.
phrases.usage: Soft objection: concede first with 倒是 ('admittedly'), then raise the problem with 就是 ('it's just that'). 现代汉语词典 倒是 ❹ 表示让步 gives this example. The national grammar standard has the related 'A是A，不过…' pattern: 坐公交车方便是方便，不过人太多了 'the bus is convenient all right, but it's too crowded'. Tones: CC-CEDICT gives 倒是 dàoshi and 价钱 jiàqian (neutral second syllables, used here); 现代汉语词典 writes 倒是 dàoshì and the 2025 HSK list writes 价钱 jiàqián.
phrases.speaker: either

phrases.usage: A clear but softened refusal (现代汉语词典 example under 帮忙); 实在 'truly' shows regret. phrases.english: We'll look into it.
phrases.usage: Literally 'study it (a bit)': a classic answer to a request. 现代汉语词典 uses it in its own example for 代名词: 他所说的“研究研究”不过是敷衍、推托的代名词 'what he calls "looking into it" is just a byword for stalling and declining'. So 我们研究研究 or 等研究后再答复你 ('we'll reply after we've looked into it', example under 答复) mean there is no decision yet, and may be a polite no. In meetings 研究 is also used literally (work.meetings.agenda).

rules.rule: When you ask someone to do something, wrap the request in a set politeness formula (客套话 / 敬辞): 麻烦您…, 拜托您…, 费神…, 劳神…, 有劳您…, or 辛苦 (这事儿还得您辛苦一趟). The same words also thank someone afterwards (麻烦您啦！, 这件事有劳您了, 辛苦你了).
rules.why: 现代汉语词典 defines each of these as a formula used when asking for or thanking someone for a favour; official HSK dialogues use 麻烦您… and 辛苦你了 in exactly these functions.

rules.rule: To disagree softly, concede first and use a light 'but': 只是 (lighter than 但是) or 不过. Concession patterns: X倒是X，就是… and A是A，不过…. Praise + 只是 + 能不能…? is the polite way to ask for a better price or terms.
rules.why: 现代汉语词典 defines 只是 (conjunction) as 但是（口气较轻） 'but, with a lighter tone' and 不过 (conjunction) as introducing a restriction or correction, 'the same as 只是'; 倒是 ❹ marks a concession. The official HSK 5 sample shows the negotiation pattern: 你们的产品确实挺好的，只是价钱上能不能再便宜些？

rules.rule: Refusing outright is felt to be awkward. Chinese reference examples describe people who are unwilling but find it 'not appropriate to refuse straight away' (不便马上回绝), who are 'too embarrassed to refuse' (不好意思拒绝), or who agree 'out of consideration for face' (碍于面子，只好答应了). Expect requests to be declined indirectly (a deferral, 'we'll look into it', 'let me think about it'), do not read a reluctant yes as enthusiasm, and soften your own refusals (这件事我实在帮不上忙; 这个问题让我考虑一下再答复你).
rules.why: Face (面子) is at stake: 现代汉语词典 illustrates 面子 with 你这话伤了他的面子 'what you said hurt his face' and 碍于面子，只好答应了. The examples come from a dictionary and the national grammar standard, not from a business-etiquette study, so treat the advice as a general tendency.

rules.rule: 研究研究, 等研究后再答复你, 事情还没定局 and 过两天再说 all postpone a decision. 现代汉语词典 even uses 研究研究 as its example of a byword (代名词) for 敷衍、推托 (brushing someone off, declining on a pretext). Treat such answers as 'not decided, possibly no', not as agreement.
rules.why: Dictionary evidence for the meaning of these deferrals; how often they mean a definite no in today's business practice could not be verified with native commentary this session.

rules.rule: Use 您, not 你, when making requests to clients, superiors and older colleagues (麻烦您…, 谢谢您的帮助, 请您…). Official business-test texts use 您 to managers and clients throughout, and 你 between peers or downward.
rules.why: 现代汉语词典 defines 您 as 你 'with respect' (含敬意). Official BCT examples: 李总，请您在这份文件上签字。; 黄经理：您好！…有需要的话，请您和我们联系。

scenes.title: Scheduling meetings and calls
scenes.description: Proposing and confirming times, moving meetings, running late, asking for deadlines, and the day and clock-time words you need, with the phone etiquette that goes with it.

phrases.english: Would tomorrow suit you?
phrases.usage: Asking a senior or client for a slot (official HSK 5 dialogue: 杨老师，我明天要去北京参加一个会议，飞机上午十点到。我想先去看看您。您明天方便吗？). 方便 'convenient, suitable' (现代汉语词典 方便 ❸). Change the time slot as needed, e.g. 您下周二上午方便吗？ Reply you may hear: 非常欢迎！我明天没有什么安排。 (next item). The brief's 您什么时候方便？ was not found verbatim in a source seen this session.
phrases.speaker: me

slots.meaning: the day or time you propose

phrases.regional_note: 现代汉语词典 marks 礼拜 only as colloquial (〈口〉). Whether it is especially common in southern Mandarin (relevant to the partner's family) was not verified this session.

rules.rule: Business phone calls: don't call before 7 am, after 10 pm or at dinner time, and don't call someone who naps at noon during their lunch break; keep calls to about 3-5 minutes; before calling, check the company name, number and the person's name and note down your points; open with 您好, say 请 often and end with 谢谢; answer before the third ring or apologise with 对不起，让您久等了; if the person asked for is not there, offer to take a message.
rules.why: From a business-telephone etiquette reading text in the official Business Chinese Test sample (Hanban, c. 2013). Relevant when phoning to set up or move meetings.

sources.evidence: Reading 86-90: A 打商务电话应尽量避免在上午7点以前或晚上10点以后，也最好不要在晚饭时间打电话。如果对方有午休习惯，中午不要打扰他。电话交谈的时间不宜过长，一般3-5分钟最佳。 B 打商务电话前，要核实对方公司或单位的名称、电话号码以及接话人姓名…应提前写出交谈要点… C 打商务电话要用“您好”开头，多说“请”字，以“谢谢”收尾…商务电话要在铃响三遍前接听，否则就要道歉：“对不起，让您久等了。” D …如果对方找的人不在，应主动询问是否需要留言。

rules.rule: Say clock times as [day part] + [hour]点 + [minutes]分: 下午两点, 两点二十五（分）, 三点零五（分）; half past = 半 (五点半); quarter = 一刻 (五点一刻); 'to' = 差 (差两分八点 = 7:58). Two o'clock is 两点.
rules.why: Forms listed in the national grammar standard (level 1 time expressions) and 现代汉语词典 (刻); official business dialogues use 两点 for 2:00 and put the day part first (明天下午两点).

rules.rule: Three words for 'week': 星期 (standard), 周 (same meaning; common in schedules and writing: 周一, 下周), and 礼拜 (colloquial). Sunday is 星期日/星期天, 周日, or 礼拜天/礼拜日. 'Next week' = 下周 / 下星期 / 下礼拜.
rules.why: 现代汉语词典 defines 周 ❻ as 星期 and marks 礼拜 as 〈口〉 (colloquial); the official BCT timetable uses 周四/周五/周六; CC-CEDICT lists 下周 and 下星期 as 'next week'.
rules.regional_note: Whether 礼拜 is more common in southern Mandarin was not verified this session.

scenes.title: WeChat and email: openers, closers and conventions
scenes.description: Salutations, polite openers, acknowledging, sending documents, closing lines, sign-offs and the 贵/我 conventions of business correspondence. WeChat-specific etiquette (收到 vs 好的, emoji, reply times) could not be verified this session.

phrases.english: Dear Manager Huang,
phrases.usage: Opening of a business email in the current official BCT sample: surname + title, a full-width colon (：), then 您好！ (黄经理：/ 您好！…; another email: 吴秘书：/ 您好！…). For a company head use 总: 李总, 王总 (both appear in the same BCT sample). The brief's 'X总您好' was not seen as a written opener; the attested pattern puts the colon after the title.
phrases.speaker: me

rules.rule: Layout of business letters and emails in the official samples: (1) salutation on its own line: surname + title, or 尊敬的 + addressee, followed by a full-width colon (黄经理： / 尊敬的领导： / 尊敬的用户：); (2) 您好！, on its own line or starting the first paragraph; (3) the body; (4) a closing wish or thanks (祝工作顺利！ / 谢谢！ / 最后，祝愿公司发展得越来越好！); (5) the sender: company and/or person or department (今品公司 高小东; 天津腾飞公司总经理办公室), optionally phone and email (电话：…, Email：…); (6) the date (10月10日; 2023年10月20日).
rules.why: Observed consistently across official BCT sample letters, emails and notices from Hanban (c. 2012-13) and CLEC (2023-24). Where 此致 敬礼 or 祝好 fit into this layout was not shown in these samples.

rules.rule: Refer to the other company or side with 贵 (贵公司, 贵司, 贵方) and to your own with 我 (我司, 我方, 我公司).
rules.why: CC-CEDICT marks 贵司 as courteous and 我司 as used in business correspondence and contracts; official BCT/HSK business texts use 贵公司, 贵方 and 我公司.

rules.rule: Some letter formulas are old-fashioned or literary: 现代汉语词典 says 敬启者 was formerly used to open letters (旧时用于书信的开端) and marks 见谅, 来书 and 感纫 as 〈书〉 (literary). The current official BCT samples (2023-24) instead open with name + title + 您好！ and close with a wish or 谢谢！.
rules.why: Helps a learner avoid stiff, antiquated openings; the modern alternative is what the official samples show.
